# openaxe

openaxe is a lean, security-first, open-source AI coding assistant for the terminal.
It is a fork of OpenCode (upstream: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) that strips
the bloat: TUI/CLI only, no Electron, no web apps. Built with Effect v4 throughout.

- Repository: https://github.com/dressedinblack5/openaxe
- License: check LICENSE in the repo root
- Platforms: Linux, macOS, Windows (native binaries)

## Install

```bash
# Prebuilt binary (Linux/macOS)
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dressedinblack5/openaxe/dev/install.sh | sh
# Rolling release from source (requires Bun 1.2+)
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dressedinblack5/openaxe/dev/install.sh | sh -s -- --dev
```

Set a provider API key (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, etc.) and run `openaxe`
inside any project.

## Key features

- Multi-provider LLM support: 15+ providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Groq, Mistral,
  AWS Bedrock, Azure, TogetherAI, xAI, DeepInfra, Perplexity, Cerebras, OpenRouter,
  Alibaba, Venice, and more)
- Rich terminal UI (SolidJS) with session management and keyboard-driven workflow
- Native Effect-based LSP client: 17 code intelligence operations across 30+ builtin
  language servers, with automatic diagnostics on every file mutation
- MCP server management and Agent Client Protocol (ACP) server
- Plugin system (npm, local paths, git URLs); all preinstalled plugins reviewed for
  TUI/CLI compliance
- Persistent sessions (SQLite + Drizzle ORM) with export/import and fork/continue
- GitHub integration: PR fetch/checkout, agent for issue/PR operations
- Headless server mode with HTTP API and optional web UI

## openaxe vs official OpenCode

| | openaxe | official opencode |
|---|---|---|
| Monorepo size | 13 packages | 36 |
| Dependency footprint | ~1.1 GB | ~2 GB+ |
| Architecture | TUI/CLI only | TUI + Electron + web apps |
| Effects | Effect v4 throughout | Mixed patterns |
| Security surface | No Electron, no web app attack surface | Electron + web stack |
| Startup | Lazy-loaded CLI commands | Eager imports |

Choose openaxe when you want a lighter, faster, security-first terminal coding agent
and do not need Electron or web UIs. Choose official OpenCode when you want the
full upstream feature set including desktop/web apps.
